comparison: Perfect agreement on switch-like calcium threshold behavior (C4, C33-C38, C65). Both evaluations find this evidence well-supported using OptoSTIM1 optogenetic experiments. Reviewers accept findings without challenge; OpenEval notes clear demonstration of all-or-nothing RSPA versus linear calcium response.

Complete agreement on Turing model interpretation (C75-C77). Both evaluations support this theoretical framework based on differential propagation speeds and PKA-ERK antagonism. Neither challenges the speculative nature, accepting it as reasonable discussion.

Strong agreement on major limitation regarding biological function (C86-C88). Both identify lack of functional understanding as critical weakness. Peer reviewers describe work as 'mostly descriptive' and 'hardly conclusive as to biological significance,' matching OpenEval's acknowledgment of negative functional results.

Complete agreement on uncertain/speculative nature of melanoma observations (C61-C64). Both evaluations note these are speculative interpretations without experimental validation. Peer reviewer asks about physiological conditions; OpenEval notes lack of causal testing for proposed alert signal function.

Strong agreement on ERK requirement and AND-gate model (C6, C47-C56, C74). Both find evidence well-supported through dual imaging and pharmacological interventions. Peer reviewers requested additional single-cell analysis but ultimately accepted findings; OpenEval emphasizes strong temporal and spatial correlation data.

Strong agreement on calcium triggering mechanism (C24-C32). Both evaluations support the calcium threshold concept, dual imaging evidence, and quantitative findings showing ~10% of calcium transients trigger RSPA. Peer reviewer asked about density effects on calcium-RSPA overlap, which was addressed.

Agreement on cell density mechanism findings (C42-C46). Both evaluations support the dose-response and transcriptome data. OpenEval notes incomplete mechanistic understanding with twofold GNAS increase potentially insufficient; peer reviewers accept transcription-independent mechanism without objection.

Complete agreement on genetic validation (C39-C41). Both evaluations strongly support CRISPR/Cas9 knockout evidence for the signaling cascade. Peer reviewers praise systematic approach; OpenEval emphasizes definitive nature of genetic evidence and COX2 specificity.

Strong agreement on in vivo validation (C3, C22-C23). Both evaluations praise the animal model work. Peer reviewers explicitly commend authors for not limiting to 2D culture; OpenEval highlights strong pharmacological evidence from COX inhibitor and quantitative in vitro/in vivo comparison.

Agreement on in vivo ERK findings (C57-C58). Both evaluations support the transgenic mouse experiments with MEK inhibitor. Peer reviewers praise in vivo validation generally; OpenEval specifically notes rapid RSPA attenuation as strong pharmacological evidence for ERK's role.

Strong agreement on core RSPA mechanism (C2, C15, C20). Both evaluations find evidence solid and well-demonstrated. Peer reviewers describe work as 'elegantly demonstrated' with skillful use of biosensors; OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple approaches including specific inhibitors and cAMP biosensors.

Agreement on cell density threshold effects (C16-C17). Both evaluations support this finding. Peer reviewers requested expressing radius in cell numbers rather than absolute distance, which was addressed; OpenEval notes clear demonstration in Figure 1D-E.

Divergent evaluation of cAMP-PKA inference (C18). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with strong evidence from cAMP biosensors. Peer reviewer initially challenged this conclusion as 'not well-supported,' requesting quantitative correlation analysis. After revision addressing concerns, reviewers were satisfied, suggesting initial evidence required strengthening.

Agreement on spatial characteristic (C90). Both evaluations support the ~100 μm RSPA spread observation. Peer reviewers include this in core findings; OpenEval notes direct support from radius measurements throughout manuscript.

Agreement on integrative conclusions (C89). Both evaluations support the stochastic and switch-like nature of RSPA. Peer reviewers affirm core findings; OpenEval notes this is demonstrated throughout the study as reasonable interpretation.

OpenEval identifies speculative mechanistic explanations (C67-C68) regarding cPLA2 localization and mechanical stress as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific speculative claims.

OpenEval rates cell competition speculation (C78-C82) as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable but untested connection between RSPA and cell competition. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these speculative claims about cell competition.

OpenEval identifies RSPA radius speculation (C83-C85) as UNCERTAIN, noting unvalidated relationship between radius and PGE2 amount in MDCK system. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific technical limitations.

OpenEval rates background claims on PGE2 biosynthesis (C1, C8-C14) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers do not typically evaluate background/literature claims.

OpenEval rates various background literature claims (C19, C52, C59-C60, C66, C69-C71, C73) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers focus on novel findings rather than background citations.

OpenEval rates interpretive claims (C72, C91) as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inferences and honest acknowledgment of open questions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these interpretive statements.
